{"self_assessment": "**Impact**
Our table built a fish: a nose, two body lines splitting round the top and bottom, and a forked tail. My part was the top tail stroke, which I traced and then looked over to confirm it carried through from the body line. By our last check, about 98 of 98 standing dominoes were connected to the start. I don't have the judge's verdict yet, so I can't say whether the fish was recognized. The outline had the telltale parts, though: the body, the forked tail and the nose. My contribution was real but small. Priya's plan and Maya's and Leo's strokes carried most of the picture.

**Execution**
I took the stroke I was assigned and laid it cleanly. I checked it by eye and reported back that the run connected. When Priya asked everyone to keep off the tail joint after her fix, I did, because extra dominoes there were the main risk. I'll be upfront that once my stroke was down I had little left to do. I didn't look for extra checks, such as walking the whole chain myself, and I leaned on Priya's and Leo's inspections. We had about 150 dominoes spare and plenty of time, so I could have double-checked the nose split or the far ends of the tail strokes.

**Collaboration**
I said yes quickly when Priya reassigned roles, even though the pad and the first plan had been Maya's. That avoided a duplicate-work argument. I kept to my lane, stayed clear of others' areas, and added a bit of cheer near the end. I speak up slowly in a new group, and I could have said more earlier, for example by offering a second pair of eyes on the joints.

**Leadership**
Priya led this one, and I was glad to follow. I didn't try to take over a plan that was already working. I didn't take any leadership initiative of my own, and I'd like to do more of that next time, starting with offering to verify the riskiest joints."}
